assumptions.statement: A BDL rule means condition ⇒ assertion (§5.13). Reading r-q008 as 'refuse RecordPanelDecision when the proposal is not Scored' is this model's authoring convention, so the Scored part is anchored on ac-q019's compiled precondition, which states it directly; the check verifies both are what the guards implement.

The performer part is ac-q019's mayPerform, a closed set (§9.2: any other performer violates business meaning), mapped by scope.actorRoles to the role the route checks (PanelChair → panelChair). The mapping is stated here, not inferred.

'Only once' is derived, not compiled as a condition: after a decision the proposal is Awarded or Declined (both terminal), and only Score enters Scored (sm-q003, closed by §5.8 R-07). The code is checked for a single decision per proposal (the decided guard, a conditional claim, adj_decision keyed by proposal).

An adj_case row exists only for a scored proposal: it is opened only in the ProposalScored handler. The scored guard is 'refuse without a case'; the correspondence check verifies the case is opened nowhere else.

A proposal's status is written only through transition() (the one UPDATE of sub_proposal.status, parametric); every outcome is a call of it, or of a forwarder, with a literal target status. Any other form is unresolved.

Cases set up their world through the implementation's own test harness (tests/support/harness.ts), in-process (Fastify inject) against an isolated SQLite file with a manual clock. The act under test — the HTTP route — and the state read — adj_decision and sub_proposal.status — are the verifier's.
Guards and correspondence are recognised textually (lexed, not parsed); a refactor they do not recognise reads as 'not shown', never as 'violated'.

assumptions.statement: BDL OrcidStatus Unverified/Verified is idn_account.orcid_status 'unverified'/'verified'; the schema CHECK admits exactly those two values. The mapping is stated in scope.valueMapping; the evaluator applies it.
The claim is R-07's closure (the declared transitions are the complete set of permitted changes), not 'terminal' alone: BDL gives terminal no closure of its own.
Cases run the real routes in-process (Fastify inject) against an isolated SQLite file with a manual clock and a stub ORCID registry, set up through the implementation's own test harness.
